messages:
Maria (AE): FYI — CoreFin wants to run a short POC to validate Redwood as a drop-in replacement for VendorX. They care about prompt parity, response shape, billing, and security questionnaire answers. Can SE + SRE pick this up?
Sam (SE): I can take lead on the prompt/response parity checks. Quick Q: do they need exact token-billing parity or functional parity (same output quality and cost predictability)?
CoreFin POC - Lina: functional parity first. We want <5% delta on key NLU intents and similar latency. Billing concern: our finance team wants mapping for token units so cost forecasting works.
Maria (AE): Lina — finance wants a worked example mapping VendorX tokens => Redwood tokens for a typical 2K-token prompt + 1K response. Also they asked about webhook retry semantics.
Sam (SE): OK. I'll draft a short mapping and run a few sample prompts. For webhook: Redwood uses at-least-once delivery with exponential backoff (max 5 retries) and idempotency keys. I'll paste the snippet we typically share.
Sam (SE): ```curl -X POST "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-1", "prompt":"Summarize: ...", "max_tokens":1024, "response_id":"<idempotency-key>"}'```
Nora (Security): I'll take the security questionnaire items. Heads up: CoreFin flagged TLS mutual-auth for inter-service traffic and KMS/HSM requirements for private deployment. Do they want Private (VPC) or Dedicated?
CoreFin POC - Lina: We want Dedicated for the POC with possibility to go Private later. KMS integration required (customer-managed keys).
Matt (SRE): For Dedicated we can provide customer-isolated GPU pool and KMS/HSM integration. Need to lock down IP allowlist — please confirm the egress IPs we should expect. We also need their CIDR for inbound firewall rules.
Maria (AE): Lina — can you send the CIDR blocks and the security questionnaire doc to Nora? We'll also need a signed AFA for the Dedicated trial.
CoreFin POC - Lina: Sent the questionnaire and CIDRs to Nora@redwood via email. Also attached a small evaluation corpus (50 prompts).
Sam (SE): Nice. I'll run the eval corpus against VendorX and Redwood, capture intent match and token counts, and post results here. Expected deliverables: 1) delta report (intent F1, exact-match), 2) sample request/response mapping, 3) cost mapping example.
Sam (SE): Quick note on request mapping that often helps: VendorX uses a top-level `messages` array for chat + role tags; Redwood supports both chat and completion shapes. We generally recommend normalizing to Redwood chat format: ```{"model":"rwd-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}]}``` This preserves role context and keeps response shape stable.
Nora (Security): On questionnaire: KMS OK, we support customer CMKs via AWS KMS or bring-your-own-HSM via our Private offering. We log key access and provide audit exports for 90/365 retention (configurable). I'll mark which answers need legal signoff.
Matt (SRE): Latency: dedicated pool targets p50 < 150ms for 1K token responses (depends on model). For their SLA ask, we should set expectations around burst capacity (can autoscale but warm-up can add 200-400ms for cold nodes).
Maria (AE): Lina: do you have a preferred go/no-go date for POC? CoreFin legal also asked for an IP/Data residency table.
CoreFin POC - Lina: We'd like to run the POC next week (start Mon). Legal wants residency info for EU and US options.
Sam (SE): Timeline: I can produce the parity report in 48 hours once I have the corpus and VendorX outputs. SRE (Matt) — can you provision a small Dedicated test pool by Monday morning?
Matt (SRE): On it. I'll provision 2x T4d pools in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, set up temporary KMS hooks and provide egress IPs. ETA: Sunday EOD for config + test endpoint. deploy-bot: provisioning job #467 initiated.
deploy-bot: Job 467 started by Matt. ETA 6h. Logs: provisioning -> initializing -> networking -> KMS attach.
Nora (Security): I'll review the questionnaire today and flag anything that needs legal. Also will prepare a short note on required SOC/ISO docs we can share.
Sam (SE): I'll run the 50 prompts against both vendors and post a short table of deltas + a sample mapping for billing. Example cost mapping snippet: VendorX charges per 1K tokens input/output differently; Redwood bills per-token with simple breakdown: prompt_tokens + completion_tokens. We'll translate with a small script and give an expected monthly estimate.
Maria (AE): Great — let's reconvene in this thread once the parity report and the IPs are up. Lina — thanks for sending the docs. I'll capture next steps for contracts once SRE confirms provisioning. :tada:
CoreFin POC - Lina: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround.
Sam (SE): Putting this on my calendar. Will post initial parity summary by tomorrow noon.
Matt (SRE): Provisioning complete. Test endpoints and egress IPs sent to Lina and Maria. deploy-bot: Job 467 completed.
Nora (Security): Questionnaire mostly done, sent back to Lina with 3 items needing legal sign-off (data retention TTL, subprocessor list, and KMS SLA).
Maria (AE): Perfect — closing loop. Next: Sam to post parity report, Nora to confirm legal asks, Matt to monitor POC infra.
Sam (SE): Parity report uploaded: https://files.redwoodinference.com/pocs/corefin/parity-report-1718012345.pdf — summary: intent F1 delta 2.7%, median token delta +3.2%, median latency comparable. Will follow up with mapping script.
CoreFin POC - Lina: Received and shared with our engineering lead. Looks good so far. We'll kick off integration tests tomorrow.
Maria (AE): Thanks team! :rocket:
